title: Edit second sign-in factor rule
purpose: Choose which accounts must have a second sign-in factor, with a reason.
summary: Choose which accounts must set up an authenticator app before they can work. Only the admin role can do this, with a reason.

tasks.title: Require a second factor
steps: Tick [[Every staff account]], roles under [[Staff with these roles]], or the other groups of accounts.
Explain why in [[Reason]] and select [[Save changes]]. You return to Security settings.

tasks.title: Stop requiring it
steps: Clear the ticks, give a [[Reason]] and select [[Save changes]].

good_to_know: The rule applies at each account's next sign-in. Sessions it did not cover at sign-in are not interrupted; a superuser can end a person's sessions in the admin console.
An account the rule covers without an authenticator app is sent to set one up after signing in and opens nothing else first.
Shared demonstration accounts cannot add one, so a rule covering them stops them working.
If someone saved the rule after you opened the form, your change is refused and what you chose stays. Reload and compare.

sections.title: Access
paragraphs: Only the admin role may open this form; other staff roles, client portal accounts and a superuser without the role are refused. It opens from Edit on the Second sign-in factor panel of Security settings, as a dialog or a full page, and returns there. Your role is checked again as your account stands when you save.

items.label: Every staff account
items.description: Every account that is not a client portal account, whatever its role, including accounts without a role.

items.label: Staff with these roles
items.description: Administrator, Supervisor, Client services, Account manager, Technical staff. A staff account holding a chosen role is covered. Administrators do the work of every role, so choosing any role also covers them.

items.label: Staff who can view patient information
items.description: Staff accounts granted Can view patient information, to the account itself or through any of its groups (a role group or another group), with or without a role.

items.label: Accounts that can open the admin console
items.description: Accounts with staff status in the admin console, superusers among them.

items.label: Reason
items.description: Required, up to 2,000 characters. Kept with the change in the history on Security settings.

items.label: Save changes
items.description: Saves the rule with an audit event naming you, the rule before and after, and your reason. Saving the same rule records nothing and shows No changes to save.

items.label: Cancel
items.description: Returns to Security settings without saving.

sections.title: Rules and states
paragraphs: Only active accounts are counted. An account is covered when any ticked part covers it. Nothing is required until the rule is first saved.

Whether the rule covers an account is decided when it signs in, from the account and the rule as they stand then, read together. A session it covers reaches only the setup pages while the account has no authenticator app and the rule, as it stands, still covers the account; recovery codes alone do not count. A session it did not cover at sign-in is not held until the account signs in again.
The form carries the revision of the rule it showed. A change saved by someone else in between refuses yours, keeps your choices and asks you to reload and compare.
Which accounts must have a second factor is the laboratory's decision. The application sets none by default.
